newsitem.title: USA: US Jan CPI up 0.1 pct, below 0.3 Wall St forecast.
newsitem.headline: US Jan CPI up 0.1 pct, below 0.3 Wall St forecast.

text.p: Consumer prices edged up slightly in January, the Labor Department said Wednesday, further evidence that inflation remains largely contained as the U.S. economic expansion approaches its sixth birthday.
The department said the Consumer Price Index rose only 0.1 percent, the smallest monthly increase since last summer, after being up 0.3 percent in December.

With the often volatile food and energy sector left out, the so-called core rate that analysts believe more closely tracks inflation over the longer term also rose only 0.1 percent, after being up 0.2 in December.
The January results were better than Wall Street forecasts that prices would rise 0.3 percent in January and the core rate would move up 0.2 percent.
The department said energy prices rose moderately although this was partially offset by a decline in food costs.
The overall January increases, while modest, followed an impressive showing last week when wholesale prices retreated for the first time in over two years, falling 0.3 percent.

Analysts have been generally suprised that inflation remained largely contained even though the U.S. economic expansion is one of the longest running since World War II and shows no signs of a serious weakening.
Energy prices rose 0.8 percent after being up 1.5 percent in December, while gasoline rose 0.7 percent.
The 0.3 percent decline in food prices was led by falls in beef, fresh fruits and and vegetables.
The department said transportation costs declined 0.2 percent after being up 0.6 percent, while entertainment was unchanged after being up 0.3 percent in December.
The department said the January 0.1 percent rise in the CPI matched the increase last June. The U.S. economy will have expanded for six years at the end of March.
